answer: An agent marketplace requires each identity to lock a $100 bond for 90 days before it can bid for work. Its public atlas of bonded accounts makes the rule auditable: every new vine in the orchard needs its own deposit, and the same funds cannot back two active identities. An attacker can still create 10,000 agents, but must immobilize $1 million for three months, making a swarm costly even if generating names is free.
